### Findings

- Inspected `landing-page-design` and `design-to-motion` at
  `a2735a3eaf092eaaffb6dc17df25de33ef3bd048`, plus the companion
  `redesign-existing-projects` at
  `7df13f6a289f4a7f91c5fe3efd70f51fd584ec28`. Both repositories are MIT.
- `landing-page-design` is a strong craft baseline but not drop-in. Its
  useful core is conversion discipline, type and spacing systems, radius
  logic, motion rules, interaction states, and the ship checklist. Its
  content-realism section conflicts directly with the business-facts contract
  because it instructs agents to invent testimonials, names, logos, and
  prices. Its font mandate and mandatory tagline section also conflict with
  the client font catalog and page recipes.
- `design-to-motion` is mostly a Figma-to-MP4/GIF showcase workflow. Only its
  website motion rules apply to client sites. It should not enter the
  client-site authoring lane now.
- `redesign-existing-projects` is a strong diagnostic for the revision and
  visual-repair lane, with the same content-realism conflicts.

### Recommendation

Integrate a curated, fact-safe craft layer: a normative standard, a shared
token module, a compact prompt block behind `DESIGN_CRAFT_LAYER`, a
report-only deterministic craft audit, and judge language. Prove it in a
three-recipe bakeoff before making it default or adding blocking rules. Do not
paste either full skill into the prompt.

Assessment written to `docs/ai-design-skills-assessment.md`. No pipeline code
or gate thresholds changed in this step. Next: user approval on scope, then
the standard, token module, prompt block, and bakeoff.
